assumptions.choice: Kept the harness-fixed broker starting cash ($10,000) and commission (0.1%) rather than setting broker.setcash(1000000) inside the strategy class.
assumptions.reason: Cerebro/broker setup (starting cash, commission) is added by the harness, not the strategy class; the spec's $1,000,000 starting capital cannot be applied from within a single bt.Strategy subclass. Commission (0.1%) already matches the harness value, so no conflict there.

assumptions.choice: Sized the buy as size = int(available_cash / close_price), i.e. floor division of all currently free cash by the Friday close price.
assumptions.reason: Spec states 'buy with 100% of available cash' but does not specify rounding or how to net out the 0.1% commission when computing size; floor(cash/price) is the literal, standard way to spend all available cash on whole shares without triggering a margin/insufficient-cash rejection.

assumptions.choice: Evaluated the exit condition (close < SMA200 with position open) only on Friday closes, same cadence as the entry check.
assumptions.reason: The entry rule explicitly says 'once a week (at Friday close)' but the exit rule only says 'once a week' without naming the day; since the strategy is described as weekly throughout, the exit check was assumed to share the same Friday timing rather than checking daily.

assumptions.choice: Used a direct comparison (close > SMA200 / close < SMA200) instead of bt.indicators.CrossOver.
assumptions.reason: Spec lists CrossOver as 'optionally' used to detect regime changes; the buy/sell rules themselves are stated purely as close-vs-SMA200 comparisons, so CrossOver was omitted as it is not required and adds no behavior beyond the direct comparison.

assumptions.choice: Used the bar's calendar weekday() == Friday (4) on the daily feed to identify 'Friday close'; if a Friday session is missing (e.g., holiday), no buy/sell check occurs that calendar week.
assumptions.reason: Only daily OHLCV bars are available (no explicit trading-week metadata); reading the actual bar date's weekday is the closest literal implementation of 'at Friday close' without inventing a fallback day the spec does not mention.
